policy: Only schedules faithfully representable by ISimulatedAnnealingCoolingSchedule are marked implemented. Broader annealing controllers remain explicitly reviewed-composite.

entries.name: Geometric / multiplicative cooling
entries.asymptotic: Exponential/geometric decay to zero for fixed 0<alpha<1.
entries.assumptions: Practical discrete cooling law; quality depends strongly on alpha and the number of transitions per level.
entries.convergence: No general Hajek-style global-convergence guarantee is claimed for a fixed alpha.
entries.reference: Kirkpatrick, Gelatt & Vecchi (1983), Optimization by Simulated Annealing, Science 220(4598), 671-680.
entries.source: Canonical practical SA baseline; retained for backward compatibility.

entries.name: Linear / additive cooling
entries.asymptotic: Finite-horizon additive decay; reaches zero after a finite number of equal decrements.
entries.assumptions: Practical finite-length schedule; beta must be chosen relative to the initial temperature and run budget.
entries.convergence: No general asymptotic global-convergence guarantee is claimed; finite-length linear schedules are included as a classical practical family examined in the annealing literature.
entries.reference: Strenski & Kirkpatrick (1991), Analysis of finite length annealing schedules, Algorithmica 6(3), 346-366.
entries.source: IBM/Algorithmica finite-length schedule analysis; linear cooling is also summarized in later SA reviews.

entries.name: Lundy-Mees rational cooling
entries.asymptotic: Equivalent closed form T_k=T_0/(1+k beta T_0) under constant beta.
entries.convergence: Published as a convergent annealing algorithm under the assumptions developed by Lundy and Mees.
entries.reference: Lundy & Mees (1986), Convergence of an annealing algorithm, Mathematical Programming 34(1), 111-124.

entries.name: Normalized Hajek logarithmic cooling
entries.assumptions: This is a shifted normalization of c/ln(1+t); the normalization fixes c=T_0 ln 2 and does not imply that c meets a problem-specific critical-depth bound.
entries.convergence: Hajek proves a necessary-and-sufficient critical-depth condition for the c/log(1+t) family under his communication assumptions; this implementation documents rather than assumes satisfaction of that bound.
entries.reference: Hajek (1988), Cooling Schedules for Optimal Annealing, Mathematics of Operations Research 13(2), 311-329.

entries.name: Szu-Hartley fast Cauchy cooling law
entries.assumptions: The temperature law alone is not the complete Fast Simulated Annealing algorithm.
entries.convergence: The original FSA analysis couples inverse-linear cooling with a heavy-tailed Cauchy visiting distribution.
entries.reference: Szu & Hartley (1987), Fast simulated annealing, Physics Letters A 122(3-4), 157-162.
entries.source: Original Elsevier article; only the temperature law is exposed here.

entries.name: Ingber very-fast cooling law
entries.assumptions: The scalar law is only one component of VFSR/ASA.
entries.convergence: Do not transfer convergence/re-annealing claims of the full VFSR/ASA machinery to this temperature component alone.
entries.reference: Ingber (1989), Very fast simulated re-annealing, Mathematical and Computer Modelling 12(8), 967-973.
entries.source: Original Elsevier article; re-annealing and parameter-specific generating distributions are deliberately not faked by this class.

entries.name: Tsallis-Stariolo generalized visiting-temperature law
entries.asymptotic: Power-law for q>1; logarithmic limit as q->1; q=2 recovers inverse-linear Fast SA cooling.
entries.assumptions: The full GSA method also changes the visiting and acceptance distributions.
entries.convergence: This class implements only the published temperature law and makes no claim to be a complete GSA implementation.
entries.reference: Tsallis & Stariolo (1996), Generalized simulated annealing, Physica A 233(1-2), 395-406.
entries.source: Original paper and its arXiv preprint.

entries.name: Aarts-van Laarhoven statistical cooling
entries.parameters: delta>0; empirical level standard deviation sigma_k
entries.asymptotic: Data-dependent; decrement becomes smaller when objective fluctuations are large.
entries.assumptions: Requires a meaningful finite empirical standard deviation from the completed temperature level.
entries.convergence: Statistical adaptive schedule; no problem-independent finite-time global convergence claim is made by the library.
entries.reference: Aarts & van Laarhoven (1985), Statistical cooling: a general approach to combinatorial optimization problems, Philips Journal of Research 40(4), 193-226.
entries.source: TU/e bibliographic record and published statistical-cooling formulation.

entries.name: Huang-Romeo-Sangiovanni statistical decrement
entries.assumptions: Requires finite level objective statistics; zero variance is treated as a frozen level.
entries.convergence: The complete 1986 schedule additionally adapts Markov-chain length and freezing detection; this class implements only the temperature-decrement component.
entries.reference: Huang, Romeo & Sangiovanni-Vincentelli (1986), An Efficient General Cooling Schedule for Simulated Annealing, IEEE ICCAD, 381-384.
entries.source: Author publication record plus reproduced statistical decrement in later technical literature.

entries.name: Triki-Collette-Siarry adaptive cooling
entries.parameters: Delta>0; empirical level objective variance Var_k
entries.asymptotic: Data-dependent decrement derived from the measured variance.
entries.assumptions: Requires at least two finite level objective samples and positive variance for a nonzero next temperature.
entries.convergence: Adaptive practical rule; the library saturates a non-positive finite-sample update at zero before applying the configured minimum-temperature floor.
entries.reference: Triki, Collette & Siarry (2005), A theoretical study on the behavior of simulated annealing leading to a new cooling schedule, European Journal of Operational Research 166(1), 77-92.

entries.name: Otten-van Ginneken adaptive control schedule
entries.formula: Adaptive temperature control coupled to empirical variance, cost scale and a dynamically determined Markov-chain length; intentionally not reduced to an isolated scalar cooling law.
entries.parameters: delta; estimated C_max; empirical variance; dynamically coupled Markov-chain length M
entries.asymptotic: Adaptive thermodynamic/statistical control rather than an isolated fixed-level scalar law.
entries.assumptions: Requires dynamic chain-length control and cost-scale information not represented by the current fixed TransitionsPerTemperatureLevel schedule interface.
entries.convergence: Reviewed but intentionally not exposed as a scalar cooling class because omitting its coupled chain-length rule would change the published controller.
entries.reference: Otten & van Ginneken (1984/1989), floorplanning/annealing control work and The Annealing Algorithm, Springer/Kluwer.
entries.source: Original Otten-van Ginneken annealing work; formula and coupling also reproduced in later adaptive-cooling reviews.

entries.name: Lam-Delosme acceptance-ratio schedule
entries.formula: Per-transition inverse-temperature feedback follows a prescribed acceptance-ratio trajectory; the complete controller is not faithfully representable by the level-only cooling interface.
entries.parameters: Acceptance/statistical estimators and feedback constants defined by the full schedule.
entries.asymptotic: Controller-driven rather than a single closed-form decay law.
entries.assumptions: Requires per-transition feedback and the complete Lam-Delosme control logic.
entries.convergence: Not exposed as a built-in schedule until the platform has a per-transition annealing controller contract.
entries.reference: Lam & Delosme (1988), Performance of a New Annealing Schedule, 25th ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference, 306-311.
entries.source: Original DAC paper; reviewed but deliberately not approximated by a misleading level-only class.

entries.name: Salamon et al. constant thermodynamic-speed annealing
entries.formula: Continuous thermodynamic-speed control uses relaxation-time and heat-capacity or energy-fluctuation information; it is not a standalone scalar decrement.
entries.parameters: Thermodynamic path quantities including relaxation-time and fluctuation information.
entries.assumptions: Requires thermodynamic quantities not represented by the current level cooling context.
entries.convergence: Reviewed as a scientifically important controller; intentionally not exposed until its required state can be represented without approximation.
entries.reference: Salamon et al. (1988), Simulated Annealing with Constant Thermodynamic Speed, Computer Physics Communications 49(3), 423-428.
